what_happened: The job asked to make the verifier's snapshot read-only, and to rerun the verifier once if the snapshot fingerprint changes. It was rejected. The verifier failed 1 of 6 acceptance criteria. The unmet criterion required a test showing that a write attempt in the snapshot (a file edit or a git commit) is denied, and that HEAD and the work-tree tree are unchanged afterwards. The one major finding was that the tests run as root. As root, the write-attempt tests check nothing, and the file-permission lock does not stop a root verifier. The tests are in run_pin_tests.rs and snapshot.rs. The event lists no failed checks.
cause: The criterion and the build's tests asserted the lock's behavior under the developer's assumed conditions (a non-root user, where permission bits deny writes) and not under the real conditions the verifier runs in. Athena's agents run as root here, so permission-based read-only locking is bypassed. The tests passed vacuously: a refused write was never actually exercised. Nothing required a protection test to first show that the write would succeed without the lock, or to run as the same user as the verifier. The gap was found only by the final verifier. This is an inference from the finding. The stored fields don't show how the build chose a permission-bit lock.
prevention: Require any test of a protection or denial to prove it can fail. The test must show the write succeeds on an unlocked snapshot under the same user and environment, then show it is refused once locked. It must fail loudly, not pass silently, when the environment cannot enforce the lock, as when running as root. Use a lock that holds for root, such as a read-only bind mount, an immutable attribute, or running the verifier as an unprivileged user. Also check the snapshot's HEAD and tree fingerprint after the attempt.
proposed_request: Make the verifier's snapshot read-only in a way that also holds when the verifier runs as root. Use a read-only mount, an immutable attribute, or run the verifier as an unprivileged user. Keep the existing behavior of rerunning the verifier once if the snapshot fingerprint changes. Outcome: a verifier cannot edit a file or make a git commit in its snapshot, and the snapshot's HEAD and work-tree tree are unchanged afterwards. Acceptance: tests run as the same user the verifier runs as. Each test first shows that the write succeeds on an unlocked snapshot, then shows it is refused once locked, and then shows that HEAD and the tree are unchanged. If the environment cannot enforce the lock, the test fails and does not skip or pass silently. Run cargo test -p athena-core and cargo test -p athena-git.
